question: What fish evidence is visible in the DMMMSU repository abstract for the La Union transplanted-mangrove thesis, and what is still missing for a species inventory?

method.summary: Reviewed the DMMMSU Lakasa repository's indexed item metadata and abstract. The browser could not open the item page because the domain blocks automated access; the indexed record describes an abstract-only PDF. No thesis text, attached PDF bytes, tables, figures or raw data were retrieved.
method.studyFinding: The repository abstract describes an assessment of selected transplanted mangroves from September through December 2021, with three fish-sampling stations. It reports an aggregate fish count for each station and says the most abundant fish sample was labeled Salotherodon melanotheron.
method.missingEvidence: The indexed abstract does not identify the three stations, provide coordinates or a named waterbody crosswalk, specify fish gear or effort, list all fish taxa, assign species to station or sampling date, provide vouchers, or expose the full thesis. The spelling Salotherodon melanotheron is retained verbatim and remains unresolved in this screen.
method.reuseFinding: No item-level reuse license or permission statement was visible in the indexed repository metadata. Treat the abstract as a discovery lead; do not reuse thesis text, charts, photos, tables or underlying data.

study.title: Community analysis of transplanted mangroves in La Union
study.citation: Asunto, M. A. (2026). Community analysis of transplanted mangroves in La Union [Unpublished master's thesis]. Don Mariano Marcos Memorial State University – South La Union Campus, Agoo, La Union.
study.availableFileAsIndexed: MT-SLUC-2026-CGS-MSF-AsuntoMA-ABS.pdf (1.55 MB); repository describes the record as Abstract Only.
study.habitatLane: transplanted mangrove study; salinity and specific waterbody type are not identified in the indexed abstract

interpretation: This is a local coastal/mangrove fish-study lead, not a verified freshwater river or lake inventory. The abstract alone does not establish whether sampled stations were brackish, marine-influenced, or in a named estuary.
The reported fish totals are aggregate station counts; the abstract does not provide taxon-by-station counts, sampling dates for individual records, gear, effort, or voucher information.
The abstract names one fish label as Salotherodon melanotheron. Preserve that exact string as source wording; do not silently correct its spelling or treat it as a resolved, station-level occurrence.
The repository lists only an abstract PDF, not the thesis body. Its full checklist, sampling protocol, exact sites, supporting tables, and item-specific reuse terms remain unavailable in this review.
No species assertions, occurrence rows, station assignments, geometry, photos, abundance-by-species values, or public app content are added. Region I and Luzon remain incomplete.

decision.reason: The institutional repository exposes an abstract-only record with aggregate station counts and one unresolved fish spelling, but no full checklist, exact sites, methods, voucher trail or reuse permission.

nextAction: Continue searching for a publicly accessible, rights-cleared copy of the full thesis or a companion paper that identifies the stations, actual sampling methods and complete fish-by-station table. Until then, retain this as an abstract-only research lead.
